question_answered_first.q: Is trust-ir's semantics written down anywhere, or only implicit in the compiler?
question_answered_first.a: Written down TWICE, and neither one is the compiler.

lean_semantics.kind: Lean 4 monadic small-step operational semantics; Semantics/Step.lean dispatches every Inst
lean_semantics.join_evidence: crates/trust-ir/tests/lean_schema_parity.rs header: 'There is no Lean toolchain in CI here to *prove* parity, but we CAN mechanically detect drift' and 'The gate matches constructor NAMES. It cannot see semantic depth.'

rust_reference_interpreter.self_description: 'Lean remains the source of truth for the full operational semantics'

question_answered_first.consequence: Agreement CANNOT be proved against trust-ir's semantics as it stands: the authoritative object (Lean) is joined to the shipped compiler by a name check, and the meaning of an emitted module in the shipped binary is fixed by to_mir.rs + LLVM. GAP 2 is therefore REDUCED and MEASURED, not closed.

executors.E1: Clean's ir_eval, discharged by the CLEAN KERNEL reducing an Eq.refl over the registered module
executors.E2: trust_ir::parser + trust_ir::interpret over the committed emitted body
executors.E3: the shipped compiled function, reached through to_mir + rustc passes + LLVM

chains.why_this_chain_matters: The emitted switch lists cases 0..9 and 11 — there is NO case 10. SourceSystem::PVS reaches the DEFAULT EDGE, and only an exhaustive enumeration puts an input on it. A non-contiguous case list with a hole is the sharpest available test of the one thing GAP 2 names by name.

chains.enum_model_note: Level carries payloads (Succ/Max/IMax/Param) elided by the harness. Sound ONLY because the body provably never reads them — enforced mechanically by ir_semdiff::payload_is_unread against the committed emitted text, not asserted.
chains.e3_absent_reason: Level::kind_ord is a PRIVATE fn (clean-kernel/src/level/mod.rs:598). Recorded as an absent leg, never re-implemented: a re-implementation would be a fourth transcription agreeing with itself.

coverage.note: Agreement on one body's instruction mix says nothing about the forms it never uses. Printed on every run; a test fails if this note is ever left claiming more than was measured.

list: assert has_cubical_layer(Cubical) = false — the Eq.refl obligations are genuinely EXECUTED
assert tag 0's answer at tag 2's value — the module does not ignore its argument
assert fuel_out at the measured threshold — the cost measurement is not vacuous
rewrite `extractfield u8 %2, 0` to `extractfield ptr %2, 1` — the payload guard refuses
assert a wrong answer on the DEFAULT edge (tag 10) — the default edge is pinned, not a black hole
falsification.structural_guard: crystal_a3_default_edge_is_actually_reached fails if case 10 ever appears in the emitted switch, so a dense table cannot silently remove the differential's teeth.

tcb_delta.why: trust-ir's parser and interpreter only POSE questions the Clean kernel answers. A wrong E2 yields a spurious RED, never a spurious GREEN.
tcb_delta.demonstrated_not_asserted: Four harness bugs during construction (missing @ sigil; functy table sized 0 vs declared functy.470; one enum declared where the body mentions enum.175 AND enum.13; subject declared returning enum.175 when it returns enum.13) each surfaced as a loud RED with the Clean and shipped legs still answering correctly.

defect_found_in_trust_ir.what: trust_ir::parser::parse_module cannot read trust_ir's own printed output for a Rust def-path name
defect_found_in_trust_ir.detail: `fn @mode::CleanMode::has_cubical_layer` fails at the first ':' with `expected '('`; the print->parse round trip is NOT total over the names the producer emits
defect_found_in_trust_ir.workaround_here: the subject is renamed before parsing; the interpreter never reads the name
defect_found_in_trust_ir.significance: independent evidence for the wider programme's move away from the text artefact as the anchor

two_design_brief_worries_that_are_actual.switch_arm_order: trust_ir::interpret returns on the FIRST matching case; Clean's ir_case_find (eval_ir_state.rs:1173) is an IRList.rec testing the head before the IH — also first-match. The last-wins behaviour flagged in the brief is in the GATE's CFG parser (emitted_cfg_parse_clean.rs, a BTreeMap::insert), not in either semantics.
two_design_brief_worries_that_are_actual.exh_flag: trust_ir::interpret destructures Inst::Switch { .., .. } and drops `exhaustive`; Clean's ir_step binds `exh` and ignores it (eval_ir_machine.rs:929). Both are exh-insensitive, so there is no divergence for a text-anchored gate to be blind to.

what_this_is_not: A PROOF. It is a measured, fail-closed agreement over a fully enumerated input set on three bodies, covering 6 of 28 IRInst forms. Extensional agreement — equal values and equal step counts on every input of a domain — does not establish that the two encodings DENOTE the same function.

does_not_move.note: Measuring encoding agreement on three other bodies says nothing about the designated target's refusing gates, and must not be reported as moving them.

enum_declaration_cross_check.why: The trust-ir side has exactly one human-chosen modelling parameter: the enum declaration reconstituted per chain, because the crate-level dump references enum.13 without carrying an enum table.
enum_declaration_cross_check.pinned_against: data/crystal_enum_tag_pin.json, produced by a DIFFERENT lane (77e42993e) from the Rust source for a different purpose
enum_declaration_cross_check.also_fails_if: a pinned enum gains a non-positional discriminant, because the harness's implicit 0..N declaration would stop modelling it
